bull_bear.body: Prioritizing R&D (39 patents filed in Q2, 587 total), inventory build for anticipated orders, and working capital for receivables; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; debt used for capex and working capital
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk on product POCs and international conversions; delay in BSNL PO issuance; prolonged high inventory/receivables impacting cash flow; competitive pressure from global vendors (Nokia, Ericsson, Cisco); supply chain disruptions
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Bullish on long-term growth drivers (5G/6G, AI backhaul, D2M); confident in product competitiveness; transparent on challenges but avoids quarter-level guidance; acknowledges investor frustration on disclosures but reiterates policy of no forward numbers
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Tejas is one of only two Indian firms (alongside Tata Elxsi) with a full 4G/5G stack; SL3000 SDR chip integration into consumer devices creates a unique D2M ecosystem moat; BSNL network is the world's largest single-vendor 4G rollout
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net Debt of INR 4,277 Cr at end of Q1FY27 (vs 3,531 Cr in Q4FY26), comprising "Gross Debt of INR 4,866 Cr and cash of INR 589 Cr at end of Q1FY27".
- Cash and Cash Equivalents (including liquid mutual funds, deposits and other bank balances) improved to INR 589 Cr (505 Cr in Q4FY26).
- Net Working Capital of INR 4,478 Cr (4,138 Cr in Q4FY26), which "increased mainly on account of increase in Net receivables and scheduled payouts"; Net Trade Receivables (net of customer advance) at INR 2,232 Cr vs 1,905 Cr in Q4FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- R&D-driven organisation with approximately 68% of workforce employed in R&D
- Ranked among the top-10 global suppliers in the optical aggregation and optical line terminal markets (source: Omdia)
- Large IP portfolio: 676 global patents filed and 371 granted as of FY26 year-end
- "Designed and Made in India for the World" positioning aligned with India's telecom self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) policy push, PLI and RDI incentives
- Deployed over one million software-defined hardware systems in 500+ carrier networks across 75 countries since inception
- Strategic partnerships with Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), NEC Corporation and Rakuten Symphony supporting global go-to-market and joint technology development
- Domestic supplier of optical and data networking products for government projects of national/security importance, including national knowledge networks and defense networks
- Active contributor to global 5G/6G standards bodies (TSDSI, Bharat 6G Alliance, ITU-R, 3GPP, TIP, O-RAN Alliance)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration and pricing pressure — MD&A flags 'limited number of large customers' and 'aggressive pricing' as a business risk; mitigation is to diversify markets and expand the portfolio into adjacent opportunities. This concentration is illustrated by a Rs 1,335 crore advance received from TCS as part of the 4G project, which will unwind against receivables only as project milestones are completed.
- Industry demand cyclicality — Demand variations and economic downturns are flagged as an industry-level risk that can affect order flow; the stated mitigation is expanding geographical footprint and target markets.
- Technology obsolescence — Rapid technological change and the company's ability to keep pace is flagged as a risk; mitigation is actively tracking technology evolution and contributing to global standards bodies (TSDSI, 3GPP, ITU, etc.).
- Supply chain / EMS and component supplier concentration — Limited availability of EMS (electronics manufacturing services) partners and component suppliers is flagged as a supply-chain risk under the company's asset-light, EMS-partner-based manufacturing model; mitigation is diversifying the EMS and supplier base.
- Talent attraction and retention — As an R&D-driven organisation with roughly 68% of its workforce in R&D, the ability to attract and retain highly skilled telecom/deep-tech talent is flagged as an operational risk; mitigated via HR best practices, skill development and competitive compensation.
- Financial market risk and rising leverage — The company is subject to credit, interest-rate and forex risks under its risk-management framework; borrowings increased in FY26 primarily to fund working capital for large project execution, and the company also carries Rs 916 crore of long-term borrowings mainly to fund capex requirements.
- Legal, regulatory and IP-dispute risk — The company faces legal and tax proceedings customary for its business, plus the risk of patent-related disputes; mitigation is contesting outstanding proceedings in appropriate forums and continuing to invest in patent filings while monitoring the market for unauthorized use of its products or IP.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Wireless: 97,500 BSNL 4G sites live; 64T64R 5G radio launched; 5G POCs in South Asia and coal mine; O-RAN partnerships with NEC/Rakuten; Wireline: BharatNet Phase-3 wins; 1.2Tbps DWDM launched; 400G/800G wins in India, Europe, Africa; 10G CPON deployed in Europe; SDR: SL3000 chip integrated in smartphones/laptops for D2M

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- The business is presented in two halves - Wireless (5G/4G RAN, mMIMO radios) and Wireline (FTTx, 100G/400G DWDM, OTN) - with Q1FY27 revenues "driven by international shipments of 5G radios and domestic shipments of 100G/400G Optical and FTTx products".
- "Registered our first commercial win for an end-to-end 5G network deployment in South America" - a purchase order to deliver an end-to-end 5G network for a South American operator.
- "Selected by a Global Tier-1 telco for a joint R&D project in 5G", and the deck cites "BSNL 4G network performance is an endorsement of our product scalability and reliability".
- Key Takeaways claim the company is "Well positioned for an AI-driven future" with a "Portfolio of products for building end-to-end high-bandwidth, low-latency networks required for AI infrastructure and user access".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [R&D/IP] "Filed 46 patents in Q1 FY27, bringing the cumulative patent count to 722 of which 380 have been granted."
- [Partnerships] Signed MoUs with IIT-Gandhinagar and MahaIT "to catalyze and nurture local innovation ecosystem in next-generation telecom".
- [Awards] TJ1600-D3 DCI product selected as a global finalist (Top-3) at the 2026 Leading Lights awards.
- [Standards/Trials] "Successfully completed field and lab trials demonstrating coexistence of D2M with cellular (LTE/NR) networks as per ToR established by an inter-ministerial committee."
- [Market drivers] Deck's Key Business Drivers cite 5G rollouts in emerging markets continuing till 2030 and "Global 5G FWA subscriptions to triple and reach ~90 million by 2030", plus data-centre, enterprise, residential broadband, backhaul and utility-network modernisation demand.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Tejas Networks designs, develops and manufactures wireless and wireline telecom and networking equipment spanning 4G/5G radio access and core, optical transmission (DWDM/PTN/OTN), broadband access (GPON/XGS-PON), carrier switching and routing (Ethernet/IP-MPLS), broadcast and SAT-IoT solutions. It sells to telecom operators, internet service providers, utilities, wholesale carriers, defense and government organizations worldwide, and also provides network installation, maintenance, upgrade and optimization support services.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Wireless (4G/5G):** 4G/5G Radio Access Network (RAN) - LTE/NR, Converged 4G/5G core, Ojas64 - 64T64R Massive MIMO Radio for 5G/5G-Advanced
- **Optical Transmission:** DWDM/OTN/PTN transmission equipment, TJ1600 DWDM/OTN product (up to 1.2 Tbps per wavelength, C+L band), TJ1600-D3 Data Center Interconnectivity (DCI) product (up to 51.2 Tbps shelf capacity)
- **Broadband Access:** GPON / XGS-PON fiber-to-home and fiber-to-enterprise equipment
- **Switching & Routing:** Carrier Ethernet and IP/MPLS switches and routers, TJ1400 IP/MPLS router, TJ1400 UCB
- **Satellite & Broadcast:** SAT-IoT solutions, Broadcast networking products
- **Software:** Web-enabled platform for remote configuration, monitoring, provisioning and management (on dedicated servers or public cloud)
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs. 1,200cr (93% India, 7% international); includes pending BSNL Rs. 1,500cr PO not yet converted to PO
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Global 5G/O-RAN expansion (Africa, LatAm, Asia); AI data center interconnect demand; 6G standardization leadership (India govt. initiative); D2M ecosystem via SL3000 chip adoption
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Industry-leading Portfolio: sustained R&D investment to cater to an AI-powered world - evolving sophisticated 5G-Advanced/6G radios with higher uplink capacities, optical products supporting 1.6 Tbps and beyond per channel for AI data-center interconnect, multi-terabit IP routers, and advanced edge products with integrated access, backhaul and compute for real-time AI inferencing.
- Using Partnerships to enhance global Go-to-Market: diversifying the customer base through strong partnerships and alliances, further leveraging the Rakuten Symphony and NEC partnerships to expand global footprint.
- Investing in Next-generation Technologies: embracing and investing in 6G and AI to remain at the forefront of technology and standards development; active contribution to global 6G standards via TSDSI, Bharat 6G Alliance, ITU and 3GPP (180+ 3GPP contributions in FY26 alone).
- Driving Operational Efficiency: accelerating process automation, quality and cost optimization across R&D, Supply Chain Management and Network Services; forging partnerships across the manufacturing value chain for a resilient and agile supply chain.
- Human capital strategy: strengthening people foundations - capabilities, systems, culture and governance - including continued campus hiring pipeline and rollout of Oracle HRMS for data integrity and process standardization.
- Continuing to invest in technology leadership, R&D, sustainability and global market expansion to keep products and services differentiated.
- The Company's Dividend Distribution Policy sets out the external and internal factors and financial parameters the Board considers in determining dividend distribution, the circumstances in which shareholders may or may not expect a dividend, and how retained earnings are to be utilized. During FY26 the Policy was amended to additionally provide for declaration of dividend in years of exceptional gains or other events.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Under BharatNet Phase-3, Tejas Networks (with the relevant Project Implementation Agencies) will deploy nearly 60,000 of its indigenously designed TJ1400 family of next-generation routers across nine states and five union territories (including Ladakh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Kerala, Goa, Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Daman & Diu, Puducherry, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Manipur), forming one of the largest indigenous router deployments in India. The company is also expanding its international footprint through customer wins and deployments - a DWDM network expansion for a Southeast Asian Internet & Cloud Service Provider, a multi-country (three-country) optical transport network for a major global sporting event, backhaul capacity upgrades for Vodafone Idea Ltd across multiple circles using TJ1400/TJ1600 platforms, an upgrade of a Pan-African optical backbone for a wholesale connectivity provider, network infrastructure modernization for a Southeast Asian state-owned power utility, and fibre access (OLT) scaling for a global telecom service provider.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- AI is catalyzing a new infrastructure super-cycle in telecom networks, reshaping network architecture with real-time edge inferencing, and accelerating adoption of higher-speed technologies (5G-Advanced, 50G PON, 800G/1.2Tbps/1.6Tbps coherent optical) - a direct demand driver for the company's optical, wireless and routing portfolio.
- Hyperscaler and AI data-center build-outs are driving terabit-scale data-center interconnect (DCI) demand and a super-cycle of optical network investment; AI-powered apps are also increasing uplink traffic, triggering 4G/5G network densification and offload.
- The global (ex-China) addressable market for the company's wireless and wireline products is estimated to grow from US$47 billion to US$55 billion over the next five years.
- Government of India's BharatNet Phase III rural broadband rollout (reaching towards ~700,000 villages) is a key demand driver; the company is one of the largest router OEMs on the program.
- India's push for technology sovereignty in telecom (Atmanirbhar Bharat, PLI, Telecommunications Act 2023, RDI Fund) favors domestic R&D-led equipment makers such as Tejas.
- Structural shift toward open, disaggregated RAN/Core architecture (O-RAN) and growing preference among telecom operators for trusted, locally manufactured equipment amid geopolitical tensions favors alternative vendors like Tejas.
- Utility network modernization (power, railway, oil & gas, public safety) is driving replacement of legacy MSPP-based networks with packet technologies (Carrier Ethernet, MPLS-TP/PTN, IP/MPLS) and 4G/5G wireless, including India's CNPN and Kavach initiatives.
- Rising smartphone penetration and mobile data usage are driving Tier-1 operators to upgrade 4G/5G backhaul networks using the company's PTN and WDM products.
- AI combined with data-sovereignty regulation is driving a data-center revolution in India, with an estimated five-fold growth in DC capacity over the next five years, boosting demand for high-bandwidth optical backbone equipment.
- Revenue mix is shifting toward international markets: India customers (government + private) contributed 84% of FY26 net revenue versus 97% in FY25, while international contributed 16% versus 3% in FY25; management believes the expanded wireless/wireline portfolio and increased investment in direct sales and support resources position the company to grow international revenue in coming years.
- FY26 revenue declined versus FY25 mainly because FY25 revenue was inflated by completion of the 100,000-site BSNL 4G project supply, and because award of certain expected projects was delayed during FY26.
- Order backlog increased from Rs 1,019 crore at end of FY25 to Rs 1,514 crore at end of FY26 (nearly 49% higher), driven by BharatNet and higher orders from domestic and international customers.
- Order inflows during FY26 were higher than revenue execution.
- A significant portion of revenue is derived from a small number of customers, which may lead to quarterly fluctuation and seasonality.
- Company continues to focus on growing and diversifying its order book through product development and international expansion.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Tejas delivered strong wireless deployment milestones (97.5K BSNL 4G sites, 64T64R 5G radio launch) but faced a Rs. 190cr inventory/warranty write-down distorting Q2 PAT; the core business momentum remains intact with global POCs and BharatNet wins, positioning it for recovery as BSNL's Rs. 1,500cr PO materializes.

risks.note: MD&A flags 'limited number of large customers' and 'aggressive pricing' as a business risk; mitigation is to diversify markets and expand the portfolio into adjacent opportunities. This concentration is illustrated by a Rs 1,335 crore advance received from TCS as part of the 4G project, which will unwind against receivables only as project milestones are completed.
Demand variations and economic downturns are flagged as an industry-level risk that can affect order flow; the stated mitigation is expanding geographical footprint and target markets.

Rapid technological change and the company's ability to keep pace is flagged as a risk; mitigation is actively tracking technology evolution and contributing to global standards bodies (TSDSI, 3GPP, ITU, etc.).

risks.risk: Supply chain / EMS and component supplier concentration
risks.note: Limited availability of EMS (electronics manufacturing services) partners and component suppliers is flagged as a supply-chain risk under the company's asset-light, EMS-partner-based manufacturing model; mitigation is diversifying the EMS and supplier base.

As an R&D-driven organisation with roughly 68% of its workforce in R&D, the ability to attract and retain highly skilled telecom/deep-tech talent is flagged as an operational risk; mitigated via HR best practices, skill development and competitive compensation.

risks.risk: Financial market risk and rising leverage
risks.note: The company is subject to credit, interest-rate and forex risks under its risk-management framework; borrowings increased in FY26 primarily to fund working capital for large project execution, and the company also carries Rs 916 crore of long-term borrowings mainly to fund capex requirements.

The company faces legal and tax proceedings customary for its business, plus the risk of patent-related disputes; mitigation is contesting outstanding proceedings in appropriate forums and continuing to invest in patent filings while monitoring the market for unauthorized use of its products or IP.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: R&D-driven Indian telecom and networking equipment company delivering high-performance wireline and wireless networking solutions ("Designed and Made in India for the World") to customers in 75+ countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Tejas Networks designs, develops and manufactures wireless and wireline telecom and networking equipment spanning 4G/5G radio access and core, optical transmission (DWDM/PTN/OTN), broadband access (GPON/XGS-PON), carrier switching and routing (Ethernet/IP-MPLS), broadcast and SAT-IoT solutions. It sells to telecom operators, internet service providers, utilities, wholesale carriers, defense and government organizations worldwide, and also provides network installation, maintenance, upgrade and optimization support services.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Tejas Communication Pte. Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in Singapore (per Form AOC-1).
- Saankhya Labs Inc. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary incorporated in the USA (per Form AOC-1).
- Tejas Communications (Nigeria) Limited — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary - a subsidiary of Tejas Communication Pte Limited; yet to commence operations (per Form AOC-1 notes).
- Tata Consultancy Services Limited (TCS) — related party: Described in related-party-transaction disclosures as a 'Subsidiary of Ultimate Holding Company' (i.e., a fellow group company under Tejas's ultimate holding company); provides IT services, consulting and business solutions, and acts as a transformation partner for corporations.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Wireless: 97,500 BSNL 4G sites live; 64T64R 5G radio launched; 5G POCs in South Asia and coal mine; O-RAN partnerships with NEC/Rakuten; Wireline: BharatNet Phase-3 wins; 1.2Tbps DWDM launched; 400G/800G wins in India, Europe, Africa; 10G CPON deployed in Europe; SDR: SL3000 chip integrated in smartphones/laptops for D2M

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Wireless (4G/5G):** 4G/5G Radio Access Network (RAN) - LTE/NR, Converged 4G/5G core, Ojas64 - 64T64R Massive MIMO Radio for 5G/5G-Advanced
- **Optical Transmission:** DWDM/OTN/PTN transmission equipment, TJ1600 DWDM/OTN product (up to 1.2 Tbps per wavelength, C+L band), TJ1600-D3 Data Center Interconnectivity (DCI) product (up to 51.2 Tbps shelf capacity)
- **Broadband Access:** GPON / XGS-PON fiber-to-home and fiber-to-enterprise equipment
- **Switching & Routing:** Carrier Ethernet and IP/MPLS switches and routers, TJ1400 IP/MPLS router, TJ1400 UCB
- **Satellite & Broadcast:** SAT-IoT solutions, Broadcast networking products
- **Software:** Web-enabled platform for remote configuration, monitoring, provisioning and management (on dedicated servers or public cloud)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Telecom operators / Communications Service Providers (CSPs) - mobile and fixed broadband
- Internet Service Providers (ISPs)
- Broadband bandwidth / wholesale carrier providers
- Data center operators
- Utilities (power, railway, oil & gas, smart cities)
- Defense and government organizations
- India - domestic government and private sector
- International markets across 75+ countries

order_book.body: Rs. 1,200cr (93% India, 7% international); includes pending BSNL Rs. 1,500cr PO not yet converted to PO

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: No specific guidance; Margin: No guidance, but international projects have higher margins; Order inflow: Expect BSNL Rs. 1,500cr PO in FY26; Capex/commissioning: Capex for product ramp-up ongoing, no specific capex number disclosed

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Global 5G/O-RAN expansion (Africa, LatAm, Asia); AI data center interconnect demand; 6G standardization leadership (India govt. initiative); D2M ecosystem via SL3000 chip adoption

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- AI is catalyzing a new infrastructure super-cycle in telecom networks, reshaping network architecture with real-time edge inferencing, and accelerating adoption of higher-speed technologies (5G-Advanced, 50G PON, 800G/1.2Tbps/1.6Tbps coherent optical) - a direct demand driver for the company's optical, wireless and routing portfolio.
- Hyperscaler and AI data-center build-outs are driving terabit-scale data-center interconnect (DCI) demand and a super-cycle of optical network investment; AI-powered apps are also increasing uplink traffic, triggering 4G/5G network densification and offload.
- The global (ex-China) addressable market for the company's wireless and wireline products is estimated to grow from US$47 billion to US$55 billion over the next five years.
- Government of India's BharatNet Phase III rural broadband rollout (reaching towards ~700,000 villages) is a key demand driver; the company is one of the largest router OEMs on the program.
- India's push for technology sovereignty in telecom (Atmanirbhar Bharat, PLI, Telecommunications Act 2023, RDI Fund) favors domestic R&D-led equipment makers such as Tejas.
- Structural shift toward open, disaggregated RAN/Core architecture (O-RAN) and growing preference among telecom operators for trusted, locally manufactured equipment amid geopolitical tensions favors alternative vendors like Tejas.
- Utility network modernization (power, railway, oil & gas, public safety) is driving replacement of legacy MSPP-based networks with packet technologies (Carrier Ethernet, MPLS-TP/PTN, IP/MPLS) and 4G/5G wireless, including India's CNPN and Kavach initiatives.
- Rising smartphone penetration and mobile data usage are driving Tier-1 operators to upgrade 4G/5G backhaul networks using the company's PTN and WDM products.
- AI combined with data-sovereignty regulation is driving a data-center revolution in India, with an estimated five-fold growth in DC capacity over the next five years, boosting demand for high-bandwidth optical backbone equipment.
- Revenue mix is shifting toward international markets: India customers (government + private) contributed 84% of FY26 net revenue versus 97% in FY25, while international contributed 16% versus 3% in FY25; management believes the expanded wireless/wireline portfolio and increased investment in direct sales and support resources position the company to grow international revenue in coming years.
- FY26 revenue declined versus FY25 mainly because FY25 revenue was inflated by completion of the 100,000-site BSNL 4G project supply, and because award of certain expected projects was delayed during FY26.
- Order backlog increased from Rs 1,019 crore at end of FY25 to Rs 1,514 crore at end of FY26 (nearly 49% higher), driven by BharatNet and higher orders from domestic and international customers.
- Order inflows during FY26 were higher than revenue execution.
- A significant portion of revenue is derived from a small number of customers, which may lead to quarterly fluctuation and seasonality.
- Company continues to focus on growing and diversifying its order book through product development and international expansion.

The company is also expanding its international footprint through customer wins and deployments - a DWDM network expansion for a Southeast Asian Internet & Cloud Service Provider, a multi-country (three-country) optical transport network for a major global sporting event, backhaul capacity upgrades for Vodafone Idea Ltd across multiple circles using TJ1400/TJ1600 platforms, an upgrade of a Pan-African optical backbone for a wholesale connectivity provider, network infrastructure modernization for a Southeast Asian state-owned power utility, and fibre access (OLT) scaling for a global telecom service provider.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- R&D-driven organisation with approximately 68% of workforce employed in R&D
- Ranked among the top-10 global suppliers in the optical aggregation and optical line terminal markets (source: Omdia)
- Large IP portfolio: 676 global patents filed and 371 granted as of FY26 year-end
- "Designed and Made in India for the World" positioning aligned with India's telecom self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) policy push, PLI and RDI incentives
- Deployed over one million software-defined hardware systems in 500+ carrier networks across 75 countries since inception
- Strategic partnerships with Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), NEC Corporation and Rakuten Symphony supporting global go-to-market and joint technology development
- Domestic supplier of optical and data networking products for government projects of national/security importance, including national knowledge networks and defense networks
- Active contributor to global 5G/6G standards bodies (TSDSI, Bharat 6G Alliance, ITU-R, 3GPP, TIP, O-RAN Alliance)

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.

hero.oneLiner: R&D-driven Indian telecom and networking equipment company delivering high-performance wireline and wireless networking solutions ("Designed and Made in India for the World") to customers in 75+ countries.
